research.title: Optimal versus heuristic entanglement scheduling: comparisons found, dependence on penalties, delays, channels largely unexamined

scope.question: In entanglement distribution networks, has any work compared optimal scheduling policies (MDP or LP based) with simple heuristic or index policies, and examined how the performance gap depends on the age or fidelity penalty function, on delayed channel state information, or on a time-varying (Markov) channel?

criterion.criterion: The paper studies scheduling or control policies for entanglement distribution that are derived by optimization (an MDP or linear-programming formulation) and evaluates them against a simple heuristic or index policy.

parts.definition: The paper itself formulates and solves a scheduling or control problem for entanglement distribution as a Markov decision process or linear program (or an equivalent optimization) and obtains an optimal or near-optimal policy; merely mentioning optimization does not meet it.
parts.name: optimal scheduling policy

parts.definition: The paper itself defines or evaluates a simple heuristic, greedy, myopic, threshold or index policy (such as a Whittle or max-weight index) and compares its performance to the optimal policy, for entanglement distribution.
parts.name: heuristic or index policy

parts.definition: The paper examines how the policy performance or gap depends on the form of an age-of-information or fidelity/decoherence penalty function.
parts.name: age or fidelity penalty

parts.definition: The paper analyzes the effect of delayed, outdated or partial channel state information on the scheduling policies.
parts.name: delayed channel state information

parts.definition: The paper models the link or channel as time-varying, such as a Markov or Gilbert-Elliott channel, and studies its effect on policy performance.
parts.name: time-varying Markov channel

claims.label: c1
claims.text: Partly. Several sources found here compare optimal MDP-based policies with heuristic or baseline policies. This search confirmed no study that tracks how the optimal–heuristic gap changes with the shape of the age or fidelity penalty, with delayed channel state information, or with a Markov-modulated channel. The closest sources report that the optimal policy's advantage depends on physical parameters instead.

evidence.title: Optimizing entanglement distillation policies via Markov decision process formulation
evidence.anchor_text: While the optimal policy consistently outperforms baseline policies such as the greedy, nested and entanglement pumping policies, its relative advantage is regime-dependent, being determined by the system parameters ( p , f 0 , f T , m ), and exhibits a nontrivial dependence on the fidelity gap Δ f

evidence.title: Adaptive Policies for Resource Generation in a Quantum Network
evidence.anchor_text: We observe that the advantage of our optimal policies over the selected baselines increases significantly with $n

review.reason: The two abstracts support optimal-versus-baseline comparisons and parameter-dependent advantages. They do not establish a search-wide absence of studies examining penalty shape, information delay or Markov channels.

claims.label: c2
claims.text: Bhavsar et al. (2026, “Optimizing entanglement distillation policies via Markov decision process formulation”) finds that an optimal entanglement distillation policy consistently beats greedy, nested and entanglement-pumping baselines. Its relative advantage is regime-dependent, set by generation probability, initial and target fidelity and memory number, and it depends nontrivially on the fidelity gap.

evidence.title: Optimizing entanglement distillation policies via Markov decision process formulation
evidence.anchor_text: While the optimal policy consistently outperforms baseline policies such as the greedy, nested and entanglement pumping policies, its relative advantage is regime-dependent, being determined by the system parameters ( p , f 0 , f T , m ), and exhibits a nontrivial dependence on the fidelity gap Δ f

review.reason: The abstract explicitly states consistent outperformance of these baselines and a regime-dependent relative advantage determined by the listed parameters, including nontrivial dependence on the fidelity gap.

claims.label: c3
claims.text: In Tacettin et al. (2025, “Adaptive Policies for Resource Generation in a Quantum Network”), the advantage of optimal generation-parameter policies over the selected baselines grows significantly with the number of entangled states required. It reaches a speed-up of up to a factor of twenty over a constant-action policy in experimentally based regimes.

evidence.title: Adaptive Policies for Resource Generation in a Quantum Network
evidence.anchor_text: We observe that the advantage of our optimal policies over the selected baselines increases significantly with $n$. In the parameter regimes explored, which are based closely on current experiments, we find that the optimal policy can provide a speed-up of as much as a factor of twenty over a constant-action policy

review.reason: The abstract states that the advantage increases significantly with the required number of entangled states and reaches a twentyfold speed-up over a constant-action policy in experimentally motivated regimes.

claims.label: c4
claims.text: The same work proposes a computationally inexpensive heuristic whose policies perform optimally or near-optimally in the parameter regimes explored.

evidence.title: Adaptive Policies for Resource Generation in a Quantum Network
evidence.anchor_text: In addition, we propose a computationally inexpensive heuristic method to compute policies that perform either optimally or near-optimally in the parameter regimes explored

review.reason: The abstract explicitly describes a computationally inexpensive heuristic producing optimal or near-optimal policies in the explored regimes.

claims.label: c5
claims.text: Halder et al. (2024, “Optimal routing and end-to-end entanglement distribution in quantum networks”) compares an integer linear program for entanglement resource allocation with a heuristic in simulations and finds the heuristic comparable to the optimal solution in all cases.

evidence.title: Optimal routing and end-to-end entanglement distribution in quantum networks
evidence.anchor_text:
Extensive simulations are performed to compare the performance of proposed ILP and heuristic. In all
the cases, the heuristic produces a comparable solution to the optimal one

review.reason: The passage describes the ILP and heuristic comparison through simulations and states that the heuristic produces a comparable solution in all tested cases.

claims.label: c6
claims.text: In Ni and Ho (2026, “Scheduling Concurrent Entanglement Requests in Quantum Networks”), heuristic, mixed-integer linear programming and reinforcement-learning resource allocation each show different advantages in simulation, in request delay, entanglement success rate, capacity use and request handling.

evidence.title: Scheduling Concurrent Entanglement Requests in Quantum Networks
evidence.anchor_text: Simulation results demonstrate that these approaches provide different performance advantages in terms of request delay, entanglement success rate, capacity utilization, and request handling rate, highlighting the trade-offs between efficiency and reliability in metropolitan-scale quantum network scheduling

review.reason: The abstract identifies all three strategy classes and reports different simulation advantages across the four stated performance measures.

claims.label: c7
claims.text: Banerjee et al. (2026, “Index-Based Scheduling for a Resource-Constrained Quantum Switch”) schedules entanglement requests in a memory-constrained quantum switch. It measures performance by the age of entanglement establishment, casts the problem as a restless multi-armed bandit, and derives a closed-form Whittle index for each request-age pair.

evidence.title: Index-Based Scheduling for a Resource-Constrained Quantum Switch
evidence.anchor_text:
In this work, we studied the problem of scheduling entanglement requests in a memory-constrained quantum switch, where
we measure the performance of a scheduling policy with the
age of entanglement establishment (AoEE). We formulated the
problem as an RMAB problem, proved the indexability, and
derived the closed-form expression for the Whittle index for
each request-age pair

review.reason: The passage explicitly describes memory-constrained switch scheduling, the age-of-entanglement-establishment metric, the RMAB formulation and a closed-form Whittle index for each request-age pair.

claims.label: c8
claims.text: Numerically, its knapsack-based index policy KAWI performed best. The low-complexity SWIS and SWID came close to it, and all three outperformed the earlier SMW and MMA policies in the settings considered.

evidence.title: Index-Based Scheduling for a Resource-Constrained Quantum Switch
evidence.anchor_text:
Numerical results
showed that KAWI achieves the best performance, while SWIS
and SWID perform close to KAWI. We also showed that all
three proposed policies outperform the previously proposed
SMW and MMA policies in the considered network settings

review.reason: The passage states that KAWI performs best, SWIS and SWID perform close to it, and all three outperform SMW and MMA in the considered settings.

claims.label: c9
claims.text: Bhambay et al. (2025, “Optimal Scheduling in a Quantum Switch”) argues that optimal switch scheduling must solve an average-reward MDP. It illustrates that the drift under the MDP solution is negative compared with the MaxWeight policy.

evidence.title: Optimal Scheduling in a Quantum Switch
evidence.anchor_text:
As introduced in the previous section, the optimal scheduling policy must solve an average
reward MDP. For illustration, see Figure 2(a), which shows that the drift of the policy
obtained as a solution of the average reward MDP is negative compared to that of the
MaxWeight policy for the quantum switch, as depicted in Figure 1

review.reason: The passage states that optimal scheduling must solve an average-reward MDP and describes the illustrated negative drift relative to MaxWeight.

claims.label: c10
claims.text: Bhambay et al. (2025, “Optimal Scheduling in a Quantum Switch: Capacity and Throughput Optimality”) shows that a sequence of Max-Weight policies is throughput optimal in the asymptotic sense. Its optimal fluid dynamics are given by a scheduler that solves an average-reward MDP.

evidence.title: Optimal Scheduling in a Quantum Switch: Capacity and Throughput Optimality
evidence.anchor_text: We then show that a sequence of Max-Weight policies that we propose achieve throughput optimality in the asymptotic sense. Our proof techniques analyse a two-time scale separation phenomenon at the fluid scale for a general switch topology. This allows us to demonstrate that the optimal fluid dynamics are given by a scheduling algorithm that solves a certain average reward Markov Decision Process

review.reason: The abstract explicitly states asymptotic throughput optimality for the proposed sequence of Max-Weight policies and characterizes optimal fluid dynamics through an average-reward MDP.

claims.label: c11
claims.text: Fittipaldi et al. (2023, “A Linear Algebraic Framework for Dynamic Scheduling Over Memory-Equipped Quantum Networks”) derives Lyapunov drift-minimizing scheduling policies for quantum networks. It benchmarks Max-Weight inspired policies that cut computation cost significantly at the price of a slight performance degradation.

evidence.title: A Linear Algebraic Framework for Dynamic Scheduling Over Memory-Equipped Quantum Networks
evidence.anchor_text:
The framework is then employed to apply Lyapunov Drift Minimization (a standard
technique in classical network science) to mathematically derive a natural class of scheduling policies for
quantum networks minimizing the square norm of the user demand backlog. Moreover, an additional class
of Max-Weight inspired policies is proposed and benchmarked, reducing significantly the computation
cost at the price of a slight performance degradation

review.reason: The passage describes deriving scheduling policies through Lyapunov drift minimization and benchmarking Max-Weight-inspired policies that significantly reduce computation at a slight performance cost.

claims.label: c12
claims.text: Fittipaldi et al. (2022, “A Linear Algebraic Framework for Quantum Internet Dynamic Scheduling”) compares a simple greedy policy with several Max-Weight inspired policies. In its model, the scheduler's information ranges from full global information to partial local information.

evidence.title: A Linear Algebraic Framework for Quantum Internet Dynamic Scheduling
evidence.anchor_text: Our algebraic model allows the scheduler to use the storage of temporary intermediate links to optimize the performance, depending on the information availability, ranging from full global information for a centralized scheduler to partial local information for a distributed one. As an illustrative example, we compare a simple greedy scheduling policy with several Max-Weight inspired scheduling policies and illustrate the resulting achievable rate regions for two competing pairs of clients through a network

review.reason: The abstract states both the greedy-versus-Max-Weight comparison and the range from full global to partial local scheduler information.

claims.label: c13
claims.text: Welling and Yener (2026, “Age of Quantum Information: Fidelity-Aware Teleportation Scheduling”) analyses teleportation scheduling of quantum status updates as an MDP. It shows that the policy minimizing a fidelity-aware age penalty function has a threshold structure.

evidence.title: Age of Quantum Information: Fidelity-Aware Teleportation Scheduling
evidence.anchor_text: Specifically, we consider a time-slotted formulation where entanglement is distributed and an update arrives independently with fixed probability in each slot, which we analyze using a Markov decision process. We characterize the scheduling policy that minimizes a fidelity-aware age penalty function and show that it has a threshold structure

review.reason: The abstract explicitly describes an MDP for teleportation scheduling of quantum status updates and a threshold-structured policy minimizing a fidelity-aware age penalty.

claims.label: c14
claims.text: Mitrolaris et al. (2026, “Age-Based Scheduling for a Memory-Constrained Quantum Switch”) adopts an age-based metric, motivated by the age-of-information literature, to evaluate the scheduling policies it proposes for a quantum switch.

evidence.title: Age-Based Scheduling for a Memory-Constrained Quantum Switch

Motivated by the age of information (AoI) literature [14],
we adopt an age-based metric so as to evaluate the performance of a quantum switch under the proposed scheduling
policies

review.reason: The passage directly states that an age-based metric motivated by the AoI literature evaluates the proposed quantum-switch scheduling policies.

evidence.title: Structural Property of the Optimal Entanglement Policy for Quantum Network Switch: An MDP Approach

review.reason: The abstract states that the optimal policy is bipartite below one weight threshold and tripartite above another in a weighted-throughput formulation.
